He emphasized that every missile received counters Moscow's actions and protects lives as winter nears. The call follows ongoing Russian aerial campaigns and comes amid debates on NATO membership and sustained Western aid, with supporters amplifying the urgency while some question the pace of deliveries.

news.hook: In Berlin and Oslo, defense ministers shook hands over agreements that let European partners tap into Ukraine's battle-hardened tech.
news.name: Ukraine Shares Combat-Tested DELTA System with Germany and Norway
news.summary: Germany signed a letter of intent to access Ukraine's DELTA battlefield management system, a digital tool for real-time intelligence, planning, and coordination refined in intense fighting. Norway advanced joint work on the Desna short-range air defense system—pairing Ukrainian missiles with Norwegian tech—and will test DELTA too. These deals shift from one-way aid to two-way exchanges, boosting European security as Ukraine shares frontline expertise while gaining industrial support and funding like Norway's $7 billion in 2026 aid.

news.hook: A U.S. Army sergeant with access to sensitive weapons data took payments to hand over military manuals and hard drives to China-linked buyers. His guilty plea in federal court marks a stark betrayal of the trust placed in him.
news.name: Army Sergeant Pleads Guilty to Selling Secrets to China
news.summary: Jian Zhao, 37, stationed at Joint Base Lewis-McChord, admitted conspiring from November 2021 to March 2025 to sell excerpts from HIMARS technical manuals, military hard drives, computers, and photos of restricted documents on operations and missile systems. He received about $15,000 in payments and was arrested at his Lacey, Washington home where agents found $30,000 in cash and Army devices. This is the second guilty plea in the FBI-investigated case; Zhao faces up to 10 years in prison with sentencing set for March 1, 2027.

news.summary: The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a breach in their open-source intelligence system, which exposed some unclassified information from public data sets. news.summary: The Lockheed Martin F-35A, call sign F35LTNG and registration 13-5067, activated squawk 7700 near Abu Dhabi on November 23, 2026, before heading to Al Dhafra Air Base. This followed a similar emergency for the jet within 48 hours and an F-16 incident two days earlier. The events overlap with Iran's IRGC claiming attacks on three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, including explosions and fires despite U.S. escorts, plus a reported U.S. drone downing. U.S. Central Command has not confirmed aircraft issues, while details of the tanker incidents remain unverified.

news.summary: Newly surfaced CCTV footage from March 3, 2026, depicts the destruction of Iran Air's EP-IEP Airbus A319 during U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets. The 24-year-old plane, one of three in service for the carrier, had been grounded since February 28 with no passengers aboard; the blast also damaged the airport terminal. While Iranian media called it an attack on civilian aviation, some noted Bushehr's dual civilian-military role and past sanctions on Iran Air for alleged military transport. The clip has brought fresh focus to the ongoing war's early strikes.

news.hook: A man in a dark suit handed a note claiming a bomb, demanded $200,000 and parachutes, then vanished into a stormy night over Washington.
news.name: 55 Years Since D.B. Cooper's Unsolved Hijacking Leap
news.summary: On November 24, 1971, Dan Cooper—later misreported as D.B. Cooper—hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 from Portland to Seattle, released passengers after getting ransom and chutes, then jumped from the plane mid-flight. An eight-year-old boy found $5,800 of the money in 1980 along the Columbia River, but no body, parachute, or the rest of the cash ever turned up despite massive FBI searches. The case reshaped airport security with metal detectors and the 'Cooper vane' on Boeing 727s, and it remains the only unsolved U.S. commercial airliner hijacking, fueling endless fascination over whether he survived the rugged jump.

news.hook: For the ninth year in a row, the Pentagon couldn't prove its books balanced on nearly $10 trillion in assets and liabilities. Frustration boiled over as people demanded real accountability for taxpayer dollars.
news.name: Pentagon Fails Financial Audit for Ninth Straight Year
news.summary: The Defense Department inspector general issued a disclaimer of opinion on fiscal 2026 statements, unable to verify the numbers despite reviewing $4.9 trillion in assets and $5.2 trillion in liabilities. Progress showed in 14 of 25 reporting entities earning clean audits, covering 56 percent of assets and 86 percent of liabilities—up from last year. Rep. Chrissy Houlahan called the streak unacceptable and pushed for more transparency, while voices like veteran Joe Napoli urged scrutiny of the military-industrial complex and stronger safeguards against waste. Pentagon leaders aim for a clean audit by 2028 with new tools and strategies.

news.hook: Jared Kushner's private equity firm quietly held millions in a key U.S. defense supplier while he negotiated peace deals abroad. The late disclosure has drawn sharp criticism from lawmakers like Rep. Mike Levin, who called it getting caught with a hand in the cookie jar.
news.name: Jared Kushner's Firm Held Undisclosed Stake in Defense Contractor During Peace Role
news.summary: Affinity Partners, founded by Kushner, acquired about 689,411 shares in Connecticut-based Arxis, valued at $32 million as of June 30, 2026, marking its first defense sector investment. Arxis supplies components for F-35 jets, Navy destroyers, nuclear submarines, and anti-missile systems, with defense work making up 47 percent of its $1.6 billion revenue. The stake appeared in an amended SEC filing on November 5, 2026—two days after midterm elections—after being omitted from the original August submission, as Kushner served as an unpaid envoy for President Trump on Gaza, Ukraine, and other conflicts. Critics question potential conflicts, while supporters call it standard portfolio management amid partisan divides.

news.summary: HungerG offers a 1M context window, multimodal input, and no training on user data, available free for Go subscribers on OpenCode and without credits on Qoder until November 30.
